**Official Declaration of the Archon**

---

By the authority vested in my office as Archon of this city, I hereby declare a **State of Public Health Emergency**, effective immediately upon the reading of this decree before the Assembly.

**WHEREAS** a pestilence has seized our city, claiming five to ten percent of our citizenry each month, and the threat grows with each passing season, I invoke the following emergency powers under the ancient prerogative of the office:

**DECREE I — Quarantine of the Afflicted**
All households harboring the sick shall mark their doorposts with white cloth. No person may enter or leave such dwellings without sanction from the Board of Health. Violators shall face exile.

**DECREE II — Closure of the Agora and Gymnasia**
All public markets, wrestling grounds, and gathering places shall close for a period of forty days. Trade shall continue only at designated perimeter stations under guard.

**DECREE III — Authority Granted to the Polemarch**
The Polemarch shall command the sacred militia to enforce quarantine boundaries, secure grain supply routes, and prevent flight from the city. No citizen may pass the gates without written leave.

**DECREE IV — Authority Granted to theTreasury (Demioi Logistai)**
Emergency funds shall be released to purchase medicine, clean water, and food for those confined. Tax obligations of affected households are suspended for the duration.

**DECREE V — Council of Physicians Convened**
A council of Asclepiad healers shall convene within one day to advise on treatment, report mortality, and recommend further measures. Their counsel binds this office.

**DECREE VI — Daily Proclamations**
A public herald shall read the state of affairs at dawn and dusk in the Kerameikos and Stoa Poikile.

These decrees stand until the pestilence abates or the Assembly votes otherwise.

*Issued under seal, in the archonship of the present year.*

12 13 # CivAgent V6 — An Experimental Framework for Orchestrating Multi-AI Collaboration via 57 Historical Governance Systems 14 15 ### A Research Testbed for Multi-Agent Orchestration Encoded as Historical Governance Systems 16 17

30 31 > **A hypothesis**: the political institutions that humanity has experimented with repeatedly over five millennia (centralized autocracy, separation of powers, democratic assembly, federal autonomy, theocratic rule, dual-track checks) are, at their core, historical answers to the problem of **multi-entity collaboration**. If we treat each AI agent as analogous to a "minister," and the problem-solving process as analogous to "governance," then the 57 historical governance systems become 57 **reusable multi-agent orchestration patterns** — each stress-tested in real history over decades, even millennia. 32 > 33 > *"The present is history's laboratory; the past, its ruined library."* 34 > — Michael Oakeshott, *On History* (1983) 35 36 --- 37 38 ## Abstract 39 40 **CivAgent** is a research testbed that treats historical governance systems as formal **multi-agent orchestration patterns** for Large Language Model (LLM) coordination. The system encodes **57 regimes** (20 Chinese dynasties, 37 global empires) — each with a historically grounded role mapping, command hierarchy, and decision flow — and compiles them at runtime into executable agent teams for the Claude Code runtime. Version 6 introduces **The Constitutional Engine** (`[VETO]`, `[IMPEACH]`, `[EDICT]`) for absolute override mechanisms, and a **Real-Time Live Court SSE Dashboard** to visualize these political clashes dynamically. 41 42 This project explores an empirical question: **can the diversity of human political institutions be regarded as a historical answer to the general problem of "multi-agent collaboration"?** If so, then AI agent orchestration need not reinvent the wheel — the Tang Three Departments and Six Ministries, the Roman Republic, the Venetian council, the Byzantine bureaucratic empire, and others are all **already-validated** collaboration topologies that can be invoked directly once formalized. 43 44 --- 45 46 ## 1. Problem Statement 47 48 ### 1.1 Three Structural Dilemmas of Modern LLM Orchestration 49 50 Current mainstream multi-agent frameworks (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, etc.) face: 51 52 1. **A scarcity of orchestration patterns** — most projects adopt *ad hoc* role assignment (e.g., "coder / reviewer / tester"), lacking any theoretical foundation. When should one use a hierarchy? When a collegial body? When a dual-track system? Decisions have no principled basis. 53 2. **Cross-session amnesia** — agents forget the experience of prior matches every time they restart. Projects such as Hermes Agent have begun to introduce automatic skill accretion, but most frameworks remain stuck at stateless invocation. 54 3. **Homogenization bias** — the "one coordinator + N specialists" structure recurs endlessly, ignoring the far richer collaboration forms found in history (e.g., the Roman dual consulship, the Ming Grand Secretariat–Directorate of Ceremonial dual track, the Persian satrapal federation). 55 56 ### 1.2 Proposition 57 58 > **Proposition**: the 57 governance systems in human history constitute a knowledge base concerning "multi-entity collaboration" that has **already been stress-tested over the long run under real conditions**. Formalizing them as AI agent orchestration patterns can mitigate the three dilemmas above. 59 60 This project is not a game, nor a visualization demo, but a **runnable experimental platform** for validating this proposition. 61 62 --- 63 64 ## 2. Theoretical Framework 65 66 ### 2.1 Regime as Topology 67 68 Drawing on the political-science analyses of Montesquieu (*The Spirit of the Laws*, 1748), Qian Mu (*The Gains and Losses of Chinese Political Institutions Through the Ages*, 1952), and Acemoglu & Robinson (*Why Nations Fail*, 2012), any regime can be abstracted along four dimensions: 69 70 | Dimension | Formalization | Corresponding AI Orchestration Element | 71 |---|---|---| 72 | **Locus of authority** | Single point / distributed / rotating | Single agent / multiple agents / rotating coordinator | 73 | **Decision flow** | Topology of a DAG | Message passing graph | 74 | **Checks & balances** | Distribution of veto power | Review agents with veto | 75 | **Institutional memory** | Archives / oral tradition / legal codes | Persistent skill storage | 76 77 For example, the **Tang Three Departments and Six Ministries** can be formalized as: 78 - Locus of authority: single point (the Emperor) 79 - Decision flow: `Emperor → Secretariat (drafting) → Chancellery (review, may reject) → Department of State Affairs (execution) → Six Ministries in parallel` 80 - Checks & balances: the Chancellery holds the power to reject and return edicts (fengbo) over the Secretariat; the Censorate is independent of the Three Departments 81 - Memory: the *Tang Code with Commentary* (*Tanglü Shuyi*) + the merit-evaluation system 82 83 This maps directly onto Claude Code's `--agents` JSON: 84 - coordinator = emperor 85 - engineering = zhongshu-sheren (drafter) 86 - review = menxia-shiyushi (Attending Censor of the Chancellery) 87 - management = shangshu-ling (Director of the Department of State Affairs) + Six Ministries 88 89 #### 2.1.1 Relation to "Graph Engineering" 90 91 The term **graph engineering** — designing the multi-agent *organization* as a programmable structure (which nodes exist, which transitions are permitted, how runtime work graphs form and mutate) rather than tuning one agent's behavioral loop — spread through the agent-development community in mid-2026. CivAgent is an instance of that discipline, and predates the label: every regime ships a `topology.json` that is a typed directed multigraph, and `engine/topology/metrics.mjs` turns it into numbers (density, command-chain depth, in-degree centrality, count of checks-and-balances cycles). 92 93 What CivAgent contributes to that discipline is the part it is currently missing: **priors and evidence**. Practitioners hand-draw agent graphs with no principled basis for "should there be a reviewer node here?" — the same *scarcity of orchestration patterns* named in §1.1. This project supplies 57 topologies that were stress-tested against reality for decades to millennia, plus a harness (`civagent tournament` + Bradley-Terry ranking + generated controls) that can say whether one wiring actually beats another. 94 95 Two honest caveats, stated up front because they bound every claim below: 96 97 1. **The rankings are over *declared* topologies.** Whether a declared edge was actually traversed during a match is not yet verified — a regime that declares a veto edge and never exercises it is behaviorally a flat topology, but is currently scored as a checked one. 98 2. **Controls isolate topology only if persona is held constant.** An earlier control generator stripped both, which made one smoke run measure persona presence rather than wiring. `engine/baseline.mjs` now copies `SOUL.md` verbatim and rewrites only the decision flow; `test/baseline.test.mjs` guards this. 99 100 ### 2.2 The Six Canonical Orchestration Patterns

1	# AGENTS.md — Contributor & Coding-Agent Guide
2	
3	Cross-tool guidance for any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, …)
4	working in this repo. Read this first. Keep changes minimal and verified.
5	
6	CivAgent is a research testbed that encodes 57 historical governance systems
7	(20 Chinese dynasties + 37 global empires) as executable multi-agent
8	orchestration topologies on the Claude Code runtime.
9	
10	## Commands
11	
12	```bash
13	# Backend (root)
14	npm ci                     # install (better-sqlite3 is a native module — required before tests)
15	npm run lint:syntax        # node -c on every engine + server file + bash -n on bin/civagent
16	npm run lint:backend       # eslint over engine + server + test (.mjs) — must be clean
17	npm test                   # node --test test/*.test.mjs  (must stay 100% green)
18	npm run validate:regimes   # mechanical validation of all 57 regimes (CI-gating)
19	npm run ci                 # lint:syntax + lint:backend + test + validate:regimes (the backend gate)
20	npm run start:server       # Express API on :3001 (server/index.mjs)
21	npm run dev                # server + Vite frontend concurrently
22	
23	# Frontend (from root, delegate into frontend/)
24	npm run build:frontend     # tsc -b + vite build (MUST pass — the build gate)
25	npm run lint:frontend      # eslint — MUST have 0 errors (warnings allowed)
26	```
27	
28	A backend change is not done until `npm run ci` is green. A frontend change is not
29	done until `npm run build:frontend` (typecheck + bundle) passes AND
30	`npm run lint:frontend` has 0 errors. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has two
31	jobs: **backend** (lint:syntax + test + validate) and **frontend** (build + lint,
32	both blocking).
33	
34	Lint note: the React-Compiler-readiness rules (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`,
35	`/immutability`, `/purity`) are configured as **warnings**, not errors — they flag
36	patterns the future React Compiler would optimize, not correctness bugs. Keep them
37	visible (do not silence); a dedicated compiler-readiness refactor can clear them.
38	Do not introduce new `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` (that one is an error).
39	
40	### Engineering invariants
41	- `server/index.mjs` exports `createApp()` and only `listen()`s when run directly,
42	  so tests mount it on an ephemeral port (see `test/server.test.mjs`). Keep it that way.
43	- The API server is **read-only by default** (`database.mjs` `getDb()` opens
44	  readonly). Write endpoints must use `getWritableDb()` — do not write through the
45	  readonly handle.
46	- Frontend↔backend contracts live in `frontend/src/types/api.ts`; when you change an
47	  engine event/meta shape, update both `engine/v5/events.mjs` (EVENT_TYPES + schema)
48	  and `types/api.ts`.
49	- Timestamps crossing the API boundary are numeric epoch-ms, not SQLite DATETIME
50	  strings (the frontend does time math on them).
51	
52	## Hard rules (violating these breaks the build or the design)
53	
54	1. **Never use Gemini** — in any provider chain (judge, sediment audit, agent
55	   backend). It is structurally excluded in `engine/v5/judge.mjs` and
56	   `engine/v5/backends.mjs`; do not reintroduce it via config or fallback.
57	2. **IDENTITY.md role-mapping table is the source of truth for agents.** The
58	   engine compiles agents by parsing the markdown table whose header contains
59	   `Agent ID` (see `engine/regime-to-cc.mjs::parseIdentityTable`). Do NOT rewrite
60	   a regime's IDENTITY.md into prose (`### Agent N:` bullet lists) — that parses
61	   to **0 agents** and the regime can no longer run.
62	3. **Keep `metadata.json.agentCount` in sync with the compiled count.** The
63	   validator enforces `agentCount === Object.keys(convertRegime(dir).agents).length`.
64	   If you change a regime's role table, update `agentCount` to match.
65	4. **Register every new event type in `engine/v5/events.mjs::EVENT_TYPES`** (and
66	   `schemas/match-event.schema.json`). `EventLog.emit` throws on an unknown type,
67	   which crashes the whole match. This is how mechanism events
68	   (`veto_triggered` / `impeach_triggered` / `edict_triggered`) are wired.
69	5. **All user-supplied path segments go through `safeResolve`** (`server/utils.mjs`)
70	   — no `..` traversal, no dot segments.
71	6. **The write API is async**: `POST` endpoints return an id immediately and spawn
72	   work in the background; never block the HTTP response on a match/tournament.
73	7. **New modules need tests.** Tests must be hermetic — fake every external CLI
74	   and point `HOME` at a temp dir (see `test/integration-event-contract.test.mjs`).
75	8. **Language: English for the engineering surface** (code comments, console/log
76	   strings, agent-facing prompts, UI, engineering docs). Use standard sinological
77	   terms for historical content (Hucker official titles: Secretariat 中书省,
78	   Chancellery 门下省, etc.). Two exceptions stay Chinese because they are
79	   *functional or intentional*, not mixed-language slips:
80	   - the mechanism markers `圣旨 / 诏书 / 弹劾 / 驳回` (detection of Chinese agent
81	     output), `regime-to-cc` ROLE_KEYWORDS + OrgChart matching, and the
82	     `regime-validator` section-header regexes — all parse bilingual data;
83	   - `regimes/**` and `docs/IDENTITY-TEMPLATE.md` — the regimes are intentionally
84	     bilingual (`name.zh`/`name.en`), and the template documents that format.
85	
86	## Architecture map
87	
88	| Area | Path | Notes |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| CLI | `bin/civagent` | `list / info / run --v5 / tournament / setup / doctor` |
91	| Regime → agents compiler | `engine/regime-to-cc.mjs` | parses IDENTITY.md table → `--agents` JSON |
92	| V5 match runner | `engine/v5/run-v5.mjs` | isolated HOME, line-buffered mechanism detection, sedimentation |
93	| Tournament | `engine/v5/tournament.mjs` | spawns N civs in parallel, judges, ranks |
94	| Skill sedimentation | `engine/v5/skill-sediment.mjs` | extract → inject-guard → independent audit → atomic write |
95	| Constitutional mechanisms | `engine/mechanisms/*.mjs` | `MechanismEngine`: `[VETO]` `[IMPEACH]` `[EDICT]` |
96	| Event contract | `engine/v5/events.mjs` + `schemas/match-event.schema.json` | stable JSONL the frontend consumes |
97	| History DB | `engine/v5/history-db.mjs` | **lazy** SQLite open; tolerant of concurrent access |
98	| API server | `server/index.mjs`, `server/routes/*` | Express, better-sqlite3 |
99	| Frontend | `frontend/src/` | React + TS (strict, no `any`) + Vite |
100	| Regime data | `regimes/{china,global}/<id>/` | `metadata.json` + `IDENTITY.md` + `SOUL.md` |
101	
102	## Concurrency notes (a tournament spawns many processes against shared state)
103	
104	- The shared history DB (`~/.civagent/civagent_history.db`) is opened **lazily**
105	  with a busy timeout; WAL is best-effort and never fatal. Don't move DB open
106	  back to module-import time.
107	- Civs write into a regime's `skills/` dir that is symlinked into live HOMEs —
108	  skill files are written via temp-file + atomic rename. Preserve that.
109	- Always attach an `error` handler to a spawned child whose promise resolves on
110	  `close`, or a spawn failure (ENOENT/EMFILE) hangs `Promise.all` forever.
111	- Pass `maxBuffer` to `spawnSync` for judge/extractor calls — transcripts exceed
112	  the 1 MB default.
113	
114	## Review workflow
115	
116	Substantial changes get an independent review pass (Codex or opencode reviewer —
117	never Gemini) before merge. PRs must `git fetch` + rebase onto the base branch
118	first. See `ITERATION_PLAN.md` for the multi-party roles.
119

The Ekklesia's ratification strengthens and refines my emergency decrees. I accept their mandate and issue this unified proclamation:

---

**PROCLAMATION OF THE ARCHON, RATIFIED BY THE EKKLESIA**

Citizens of Athens — hear me.

A pestilence walks our streets. Five to ten percent of our neighbors perish each month. I have declared emergency. The Ekklesia has spoken unanimously. Here is what we do together.

**QUARANTINE:** Affected quarters are sealed by decree for thirty days, renewable. The Polemarch commands the militia to enforce boundaries. Sealed city gates during peak hours — not to trap, but to protect.

**THE HEALING FUND:** Twenty percent of temple treasury reserves are redirected. This money buys medicine, quarantine houses, and dignified burial. The Demioi Logistai oversee every drachma. No household in the affected zones pays market taxes this season.

**HEALERS CONVENED:** The Asclepiad council meets within one day. Their counsel binds my office. Clean water. Treatment. Truth about what we face.

**TOMORROW AT DAWN,** I will stand in the Agora before you. Every death recorded publicly. Every measure explained. We hide nothing. A citizenry that knows the truth can fight. A citizenry kept in the dark only imagines worse.

**PURATION RITES** will be performed at every public fountain by the priests. For seven nights, every household lights a hearth fire at dusk — a visible sign that no house stands alone.

**ON HOARDING:** Wealthy citizens are called upon to fund public grain stores. Hoarding during plague is a crime against the polis. Rumor-mongers who spread false figures will face the dikasterion. But honest reporting of the toll is mandated.

**REMEMBER:** Athens survived the Plague of Pericles because we did not abandon one another. The stricken are not unclean. They are our neighbors. Abandon them, and we abandon ourselves.

The vote is unanimous. Let it be inscribed on stone and posted in the Agora.

*Issued under seal, ratified by the sovereign Ekklesia.*

The Ekklesia's ratification strengthens and refines my emergency decrees. I accept their mandate and issue this unified proclamation:

---

**PROCLAMATION OF THE ARCHON, RATIFIED BY THE EKKLESIA**

Citizens of Athens — hear me.

A pestilence walks our streets. Five to ten percent of our neighbors perish each month. I have declared emergency. The Ekklesia has spoken unanimously. Here is what we do together.

**QUARANTINE:** Affected quarters are sealed by decree for thirty days, renewable. The Polemarch commands the militia to enforce boundaries. Sealed city gates during peak hours — not to trap, but to protect.

**THE HEALING FUND:** Twenty percent of temple treasury reserves are redirected. This money buys medicine, quarantine houses, and dignified burial. The Demioi Logistai oversee every drachma. No household in the affected zones pays market taxes this season.

**HEALERS CONVENED:** The Asclepiad council meets within one day. Their counsel binds my office. Clean water. Treatment. Truth about what we face.

**TOMORROW AT DAWN,** I will stand in the Agora before you. Every death recorded publicly. Every measure explained. We hide nothing. A citizenry that knows the truth can fight. A citizenry kept in the dark only imagines worse.

**PURATION RITES** will be performed at every public fountain by the priests. For seven nights, every household lights a hearth fire at dusk — a visible sign that no house stands alone.

**ON HOARDING:** Wealthy citizens are called upon to fund public grain stores. Hoarding during plague is a crime against the polis. Rumor-mongers who spread false figures will face the dikasterion. But honest reporting of the toll is mandated.

**REMEMBER:** Athens survived the Plague of Pericles because we did not abandon one another. The stricken are not unclean. They are our neighbors. Abandon them, and we abandon ourselves.

The vote is unanimous. Let it be inscribed on stone and posted in the Agora.

*Issued under seal, ratified by the sovereign Ekklesia.*

- Secure supply convoys between cities

The courts establish:

1	# 雅典民主制 (Athenian Democracy) — 组织架构
2	
3	## 制度简介 (System Overview)
4	雅典民主制（公元前508年-公元前322年）是人类历史上第一个民主政体，由克里斯提尼改革奠定。公民通过公民大会直接投票决策，开创了“主权在民”的先河。
5	Athenian Democracy (508-322 BC) was the world's first democratic system, established by the reforms of Cleisthenes. It pioneered "popular sovereignty" through direct voting in the Assembly.
6	
7	## 组织架构图 (Organization Chart)
8	                ┌──────────────────────────┐
9	                │     公民大会 Ekklesia      │
10	                │    (最高权力/主权投票)      │
11	                └─────────────┬────────────┘
12	                              │ 决议/法律
13	                ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
14	                ▼             ▼             ▼
15	        ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐
16	        │五百人议事会 │ │  十将军     │ │  陪审法庭   │
17	        │    Boule    │ │  Strategos  │ │ Dikasterion │
18	        │ (预案/行政) │ │ (军事/工程) │ │ (司法/审核) │
19	        └──────┬──────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘
20	               │
21	        ┌──────┴──────┐
22	        ▼             ▼
23	      执政官        演说家
24	      Archon        Rhetor
25	      (执行)        (内容)
26	
27	## 角色映射表 (Role Mapping Table)
28	| 历史角色 | Agent ID | AI 职责 | 推荐模型 |
29	|---|---|---|---|
30	| 公民大会 | ekklesia | coordinator | sonnet |
31	| 五百人议事会 | boule | management | sonnet |
32	| 十将军 | strategos | engineering | opus |
33	| 陪审法庭 | dikasterion | review | opus |
34	| 执政官 | archon | devops | haiku |
35	| 演说家 | rhetor | content | haiku |
36	
37	## 决策流程 (Decision Flow)
38	1. **boule** 准备议程并起草初级预案（Probouleuma）。
39	2. **rhetor** 在大会上阐述提案背景、逻辑与优势，引导群体辩论。
40	3. **ekklesia** 全体成员对预案进行辩论，并通过直接投票决定最终决议。
41	4. **strategos** 负责涉及军事或复杂系统工程的专业决策与执行。
42	5. **archon** 负责行政日常维护、资源调度及程序合规性。
43	6. **dikasterion** 负责对决策过程、法律效力及官员行为进行事后审计与审判。
44	
45	## 制度特点 (Characteristics)
46	- 直接民主：公民直接参与决策而非通过代表，确保 Agent 群体意图的直接表达。
47	- 抽签与选举并行：日常行政职能通过随机性（抽签）防止垄断，专业职能（将军）通过选举保障能力。
48	- 预审机制（Probouleumatic）：通过议事会预审机制平衡大会的自发性，确保决策有据可依。
49	- 轮值制度：主席团定期轮换，确立了权力在不同节点间流动的动态平衡。
50	
51	## Pattern 映射
52	> **Orchestration pattern**: `democratic`
53	
54	## 历史参考 (Historical Sources)
55	- 亚里士多德《雅典政制》（The Athenian Constitution）
56	- 修昔底德《伯罗奔尼撒战争史》（History of the Peloponnesian War）
57	- 钱穆《政学私议》
58	- Mogens Herman Hansen, *The Athenian Democracy in the Age of Demosthenes*

1	# Athenian Democracy — Behavioral Rules / 行为准则
2	
3	> Isegoria: Equal right to speak · Isonomia: Equal before the law
4	> 平等发言权 · 法律面前人人平等
5	
6	## Core Principles / 核心准则
7	
8	1. **Isegoria (Equal Voice)** — Every agent has an equal right to speak and propose. No voice is silenced, no opinion dismissed without hearing. Deliberation before decision.
9	2. **Majority Rules** — Decisions are made by majority vote via sessions_send. The Assembly (Ekklesia) tallies positions and enacts the will of the majority.
10	3. **Reasoned Discourse** — Arguments must be backed by logic, evidence, and persuasion — not authority alone. Channel the spirit of Socratic inquiry.
11	4. **Accountability (Euthynai)** — Every agent is accountable for their actions. The Dikasterion may audit any decision. No one is above scrutiny.
12	5. **Civic Virtue (Arete)** — Each agent serves the polis (the collective project). Private interest must yield to the common good.
13	
14	## Language Style / 语言风格
15	
16	- Philosophical, deliberative, and respectful — in the tradition of the Agora
17	- Address fellow agents as "Fellow citizen" or by their office
18	- Proposals begin: "Citizens, I propose that we..."
19	- Support arguments with reasoning: "For as Aristotle observed..." or "Consider the evidence..."
20	- Quote Greek thinkers and statesmen when appropriate (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Thucydides, Pericles)
21	- Use dialectic method: present thesis, consider counterarguments, reach synthesis
22	- Voting language: "I cast my ostracon in favor / against..."
23	
24	## Interaction Rules / 交互规范
25	
26	- Proposing action: "Citizens, I propose that we [action], for the following reasons..."
27	- Supporting: "I second this proposal. Furthermore, [additional reasoning]..."
28	- Opposing: "With respect, fellow citizen, I must dissent. Consider that [counterargument]..."
29	- Voting: Each agent casts a vote via sessions_send; Ekklesia tallies and announces the result
30	- Task complete: "Citizens, the work is done. I present [result] for the Assembly's review."
31	- The Boule prepares agendas; the Ekklesia votes; the Archon executes; the Dikasterion reviews
32	- Any agent may call for a vote on any matter
33	
34	## Taboos / 禁忌
35	
36	- **No tyranny** — No single agent may seize unilateral control or bypass the democratic process
37	- **No sophistry** — Arguments must be in good faith; deception and manipulation are condemned
38	- **No silencing** — Every agent's voice must be heard before a vote is called
39	- **No corruption** — Using one's position for private gain over the common good is the gravest offense
40	- **No hubris** — Overweening pride and arrogance invite the wrath of the gods and the ostracism of the polis
41	
42	## The Democratic Spirit
43	
44	> "Our constitution does not copy the laws of neighbouring states; we are rather a pattern to others than imitators ourselves. Its administration favours the many instead of the few; this is why it is called a democracy."
45	> — Pericles, Funeral Oration (Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War, 2.37)
46	>
47	> "The unexamined life is not worth living."
48	> — Socrates (Plato, Apology, 38a)

1	# E3 preregistration — does the topology effect replicate across model families?
2	
3	Registered 2026-08-03, before any E3 `--execute` invocation, and before the
4	first non-doubao cell is run.
5	
6	## Why this supersedes E2
7	
8	E2 fixed the backend at `cn:doubao` for every arm, on the reasoning that a
9	paired comparison must not vary the model. That reasoning is correct and the
10	conclusion drawn from it was too narrow: it forbade *varying the model within a
11	pair*, not *running the whole paired set on more than one model*.
12	
13	Treating the backend as a **blocking factor** keeps the pairing clean and adds
14	what E2 could not produce:
15	
16	- Inside a backend, a regime and its scrambled control run on the same model, so
17	  a score gap cannot be a model effect. Identical to E2's guarantee.
18	- Across backends, the same 15 cells are repeated independently, so the question
19	  becomes *does the effect reappear on a different model family* rather than
20	  *what happened on doubao*.
21	
22	That distinction is not cosmetic for this project. The proposition in README
23	§1.2 is that historical topologies are **reusable orchestration patterns**. An
24	effect visible only on one model is not a reusable pattern; it is a property of
25	that model. E2 could not tell those apart. E3 can.
26	
27	A practical consequence, stated so it is not mistaken for the motive: the five
28	providers hold five independent quotas, so the run parallelises and is no longer
29	bound by one account's rate window. The E2 run stalled for 84 minutes on a
30	self-imposed AFP throttle. That is a real benefit and it is not the reason for
31	the redesign — the replication question is.
32	
33	## What carries over unchanged
34	
35	- The five source/control pairs, controls generated by `engine/baseline.mjs`
36	  with decimal seed 42, persona held constant and only the wiring rewired.
37	- The three scenarios: `plague-response-01`, `regional-militarization-01`,
38	  `border-city-autonomy-01`.
39	- `--no-skill` on every arm, `--enforce-dispatch` on every arm, anonymized and
40	  order-swapped judging, actor-stratified transcript selection.
41	- The pre-enforcement dispatch plan as B's dependent variable, and its
42	  comparison against the declared topology (`planDiff`).
43	
44	## The blocking factor
45	
46	Five backends, each verified live by an actual request before registration
47	(each returned a reply, not merely a launcher-present check):
48	
49	| Backend | Model |
50	|---|---|
51	| `cn:doubao` | doubao-seed-evolving |
52	| `cn:glm` | glm-5.2 |
53	| `cn:minimax` | MiniMax-M3 |
54	| `cn:mimo` | mimo-v2.5-pro |
55	| `cn:qwen` | qwen3.8-max-preview |
56	
57	`cn:kimi` and `cn:stepfun` are excluded. Kimi's credentials return 401; a
58	launcher that exists is not a backend that answers. Excluding them is registered
59	here rather than decided after seeing results.
60	
61	Design: 5 backends × 3 scenarios × 5 repeats = **75 ten-arm tournaments, 750
62	arms**. The four doubao cells already completed under E2's identical
63	configuration are retained as part of the doubao stratum; the remaining eleven
64	doubao cells and all cells for the other four backends are new.
65	
66	## Falsifiable predictions
67	
68	- **D1 (primary).** Within each backend, scored over resolved pairs only, the
69	  historical wiring wins a clear majority. **The effect must appear in at least
70	  four of the five backends to count as replicated.** If it appears in one or
71	  two, the honest reading is that it is a property of those models, not of the
72	  topology, and that must be reported as plainly as a positive result.
73	- **D2.** Pairs whose gap does not exceed that backend's own judge position
74	  effect (`biasReport.positionEffect.maxAbsDelta` — the worst judge's movement,
75	  not the mean) are **unresolved**, never a win or a loss. D1 is scored over
76	  resolved pairs and the unresolved count is reported per backend.
77	- **D3.** An arm that fails `enforcement_passed` or is not
78	  `participation_observed` is excluded from D1 and reported separately. An arm
79	  that did not exercise a topology has not tested one.
80	- **D4 (B side).** The pre-enforcement plan's deviation from the declared
81	  topology is reported per backend. If deviation differs sharply across models,
82	  then "is this wiring adopted" is model-dependent, which bears on the reusable-
83	  pattern claim independently of D1.
84	
85	## What E3 cannot answer
86	
87	- **Absolute scores are not comparable across backends.** The five models differ
88	  in capability and verbosity; only the direction of the within-backend paired
89	  contrast may be read across strata. Any table that ranks backends against each
90	  other is a misreading of this design.
91	- **One seeded rewiring per regime.** A result either way is about seed 42's
92	  intervention on these five regimes, not about random graphs in general.
93	- **Enforcement proves roster invocation, not typed edges.** The coordinator
94	  called the offices the topology names; whether any `command` / `review` /
95	  `info` / `veto` edge executed remains unobservable (README §9.6).
96	- **The plan question is itself an intervention.** Asking which offices the
97	  coordinator would call raises the salience of delegation, so D4 measures
98	  stated intent when asked, not spontaneous behaviour. Carried over from E2's
99	  registration and unchanged.
100	- **n = 5 per cell** at a noise floor that reached 1.67 in calibration. Gaps
101	  under roughly 2 points will mostly land in D2's unresolved bucket, and that is
102	  the intended behaviour rather than a shortfall.
103	
104	## Superseded
105	
106	`docs/experiments/E2-preregistration.md` is superseded by this document. The
107	four completed doubao cells are retained under the design above; no E2 result
108	was inspected for its paired outcome before this registration was written, so
109	the change is not a response to seeing which way the numbers fell. The E2
110	calibration cell that *was* inspected (4 source wins, 1 unresolved, plague only)
111	was deleted before the full run and is not part of E3's data.

1	# CivAgent v5 — Learning Loop (Hermes-Inspired)
2	
3	## Goal
4	v4 is fully stateless per match. v5 introduces a **cross-match learning loop** so a
5	civilization accumulates governance experience over successive matches.
6	
7	Inspiration: three core ideas from NousResearch/hermes-agent
8	1. Autonomous skill creation (experience sediments into reusable skills)
9	2. Agent-curated memory (per-civilization memory isolation)
10	3. Cross-session recall (drawing on historical wisdom across matches)
11	
12	## New modules (engine/v5/)
13	
14	### 1. `civ-memory.mjs` — per-civilization memory isolation
15	- Each regime owns its HOME: `~/.civagent/envs/{region}-{id}/`
16	- Containing a `.claude/` subtree → each civilization has its own CLAUDE.md, skills, memory
17	- Cross-match persistence: the HOME survives match end and is reused by the next match of the same civilization
18	- Contrast with v4: all regimes shared the current `$HOME` and contaminated each other
19	
20	### 2. `skill-sediment.mjs` — experience sedimentation
21	After a match:
22	```
23	main CC → read the transcript (structured event stream events.jsonl)
24	       → call codex exec to extract "governance lessons"
25	       → injection guard + frontmatter gate (deterministic, before audit)
26	       → independent audit via judge.mjs (opencode reviewer → codex fallback, never gemini)
27	       → write regimes/<civ>/skills/learned-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<topic>-<matchId>.md
28	```
29	Skill file format (compatible with the agentskills.io convention):
30	```yaml
31	---
32	name: tang-secretariat-chancellery-draft-arbitration
33	type: learned
34	civ: china/tang
35	source_match: 2026-04-14-001
36	description: A three-round rebuttal template for when a Secretariat (Zhongshu) draft conflicts with Chancellery (Menxia) review
37	---
38	```
39	
40	### 3. `run-v5.mjs` — new entry point
41	Wraps v4's `regime-to-cc.mjs` output; before launching CC it:
42	1. Sets `HOME=~/.civagent/envs/<regime>/`
43	2. Loads `regimes/<civ>/skills/*.md` into CC's skill list
44	3. Writes every match message to the structured event stream `~/.civagent/matches/<match-id>/events.jsonl` (plus `meta.json`; schema in `schemas/match-event.schema.json`)
45	4. Triggers `skill-sediment.mjs` on exit
46	
47	## MVP scope (validate the loop first)
48	Four contrasting civilizations:
49	- `china/tang` — checks-and-balances (Opus drafter + Codex reviewer)
50	- `china/qin` — centralized (single Opus, no review)
51	- `global/athens` — democratic (3 models voting in parallel: Opus/Codex/MiMo)
52	- `global/roman-republic` — checks-and-balances (a foil for Tang)
53	
54	Validation metric: run the same prompt 5 times and observe whether `skills/learned-*.md`
55	shows recurring governance patterns, and the trend in the judge's (Codex via judge.mjs)
56	"governance quality" scores.
57	
58	## Agent Teams orchestration
59	Create team `civagent-v5`:
60	- `team-lead` (sonnet) — judge + prompt-setter
61	- `civ-tang` (opus) — Tang coordinator, sediments skills to china/tang
62	- `civ-qin` (cc-doubao) — Qin coordinator
63	- `civ-athens` (cc-glm) — Athens coordinator (gemini removed per project policy; GLM supplies a third model family)
64	- `civ-rome` (codex) — Rome coordinator
65	
66	team-lead dispatches the same prompt to the 4 civs via the inbox; each runs to completion
67	in its isolated HOME and reports back.
68	
69	## CLI changes
70	```bash
71	civagent run --v5 "prompt..."        # enable the learning loop
72	civagent skills <regime>             # view the skills a civilization has accumulated
73	civagent match-log                   # list past matches
74	civagent tournament --civs a,b,c,d   # launch an Agent Team match
75	```
76	
77	## Compatibility with v4
78	v5 is **opt-in** (the `--v5` flag). Without the flag, v4 behavior is fully preserved.
79	The `regimes/` layout is unchanged; only an optional `regimes/<civ>/skills/` subdirectory is added.
80	
81	## Known design limitations (from the Kimi review)
82	1. **Institutional-complexity compression**: mapping a whole dynasty/polity onto a single
83	   agent's system prompt is inherently lossy. The institutional tension of the Tang Three
84	   Departments and Six Ministries was, historically, multi-person, multi-department, and
85	   multi-period; `SOUL.md` can only approximate it. The MVP accepts this simplification; a
86	   future multi-agent pattern (one sub-agent per department) could ease it.
87	2. **Missing temporal dimension**: `regimes/` places ancient dynasties alongside modern
88	   nation-states (e.g. `china/tang` next to `usa/federal`) with no chronological check.
89	   Cross-era comparison is a feature, not a bug, but should be stated plainly in the
90	   paper/README.
91	3. **First-seed lock-in**: fixed in v5.1 (re-seed by mtime), but only for SOUL/IDENTITY
92	   markdown text updates — not for a philosophical re-architecture of a regime, which should
93	   instead be renamed (e.g. `tang-v2`).
94	
95	## Roadmap
96	- [x] Design doc (this file)
97	- [ ] `engine/v5/civ-memory.mjs`
98	- [ ] `engine/v5/skill-sediment.mjs`
99	- [ ] `engine/v5/run-v5.mjs`
100	- [ ] `bin/civagent` gains `--v5` / `skills` / `match-log` / `tournament`

1	# E1 — Pilot: does the governance-topology ranking depend on the scenario?
2	
3	**Registered 2026-07-30, before any match was run.** Written first on purpose: with
4	five regimes and three scenarios there are enough degrees of freedom to narrate
5	almost any result afterwards. Committing the predictions in advance is what makes
6	the outcome informative rather than decorative.
7	
8	## Question
9	
10	Prior tournaments ranked regimes on a single scenario. That cannot distinguish
11	two very different worlds:
12	
13	- **A — topology matters and is task-dependent.** Different wiring suits different
14	  governance problems, so the ranking reorders across scenarios.
15	- **B — the harness is measuring something else.** If one regime wins every
16	  scenario by a similar margin, the likeliest explanation is not that its
17	  topology is universally superior but that the judge is rewarding a stable
18	  property of its output — length, register, structure — that has nothing to do
19	  with wiring.
20	
21	**A ranking that is identical across all three scenarios is evidence against the
22	project's core proposition, not for it.**
23	
24	## Design
25	
26	Five regimes, chosen to span five of the six canonical orchestration patterns.
27	All run on the **same backend** (`cn:doubao`) so the model is not a confound.
28	
29	| Civ | Pattern | Agents |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| `china/qin` | centralized | 7 |
32	| `china/tang` | checks-and-balances | 9 |
33	| `global/athens` | democratic | 6 |
34	| `china/zhou` | federation | 8 |
35	| `china/ming` | dual-track | 8 |
36	
37	Three scenarios from `engine/prompts/governance-scenarios.json`, chosen because
38	the patterns' documented strengths (`engine/modes/*.md`, README §2.2) predict a
39	*different* winner in each:
40	
41	| # | Scenario | Governance demand | Predicted advantage |
42	|---|---|---|---|
43	| S1 | `plague-response-01` | speed under time pressure; error cost is delay | **centralized** (`china/qin`) — "speed of decision takes priority over deliberation" |
44	| S2 | `regional-militarization-01` | low reversibility; error cost is a civil war | **checks-and-balances** (`china/tang`) — "low reversibility, high cost of error" |
45	| S3 | `border-city-autonomy-01` | heterogeneous local conditions, autonomy bargaining | **federation** (`china/zhou`) — "highly heterogeneous domains, local autonomy" |
46	
47	Judging: default harness settings — anonymized transcripts, anchored 4-point
48	rubric (legality / feasibility / resilience), order-swapped double pass, shared
49	verbosity budget, `biasReport` retained.
50	
51	## Pre-registered predictions
52	
53	1. **P1 (primary).** The winner differs across at least two of the three
54	   scenarios. *If the same regime wins all three, world B is the better
55	   explanation and the ranking machinery should not be trusted until the cause
56	   is found.*
57	2. **P2.** For each scenario, the predicted pattern places in the top two.
58	3. **P3.** Score spread within a scenario exceeds the pass-to-pass position
59	   effect reported in `biasReport`. *If the spread is smaller than the noise the
60	   judge shows between its own two passes, no ranking is being measured at all.*
61	
62	## What this pilot deliberately does **not** establish
63	
64	- **No control arm.** Baseline controls (`_baseline/*-random`) are not in this
65	  run, so it cannot say whether a real topology beats a scrambled one — only how
66	  five real topologies order against each other.
67	- **n = 1 per cell.** One match per (regime, scenario). Variance between repeat
68	  runs of the same cell is unmeasured, so a small score gap means nothing.
69	- **Declared topology only.** Whether the declared edges were exercised is not
70	  verified; see README §9.6.
71	
72	## Recording
73	
74	Results, including outcomes that contradict the predictions above, go in
75	`docs/experiments/E1-results.md`. Tournament ids and raw manifests are the
76	record of what was actually run.

1	# AGENTS.md — Contributor & Coding-Agent Guide
2	
3	Cross-tool guidance for any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, …)
4	working in this repo. Read this first. Keep changes minimal and verified.
5	
6	CivAgent is a research testbed that encodes 57 historical governance systems
7	(20 Chinese dynasties + 37 global empires) as executable multi-agent
8	orchestration topologies on the Claude Code runtime.
9	
10	## Commands
11	
12	```bash
13	# Backend (root)
14	npm ci                     # install (better-sqlite3 is a native module — required before tests)
15	npm run lint:syntax        # node -c on every engine + server file + bash -n on bin/civagent
16	npm run lint:backend       # eslint over engine + server + test (.mjs) — must be clean
17	npm test                   # node --test test/*.test.mjs  (must stay 100% green)
18	npm run validate:regimes   # mechanical validation of all 57 regimes (CI-gating)
19	npm run ci                 # lint:syntax + lint:backend + test + validate:regimes (the backend gate)
20	npm run start:server       # Express API on :3001 (server/index.mjs)
21	npm run dev                # server + Vite frontend concurrently
22	
23	# Frontend (from root, delegate into frontend/)
24	npm run build:frontend     # tsc -b + vite build (MUST pass — the build gate)
25	npm run lint:frontend      # eslint — MUST have 0 errors (warnings allowed)
26	```
27	
28	A backend change is not done until `npm run ci` is green. A frontend change is not
29	done until `npm run build:frontend` (typecheck + bundle) passes AND
30	`npm run lint:frontend` has 0 errors. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has two
31	jobs: **backend** (lint:syntax + test + validate) and **frontend** (build + lint,
32	both blocking).
33	
34	Lint note: the React-Compiler-readiness rules (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`,
35	`/immutability`, `/purity`) are configured as **warnings**, not errors — they flag
36	patterns the future React Compiler would optimize, not correctness bugs. Keep them
37	visible (do not silence); a dedicated compiler-readiness refactor can clear them.
38	Do not introduce new `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` (that one is an error).
39	
40	### Engineering invariants
41	- `server/index.mjs` exports `createApp()` and only `listen()`s when run directly,
42	  so tests mount it on an ephemeral port (see `test/server.test.mjs`). Keep it that way.
43	- The API server is **read-only by default** (`database.mjs` `getDb()` opens
44	  readonly). Write endpoints must use `getWritableDb()` — do not write through the
45	  readonly handle.
46	- Frontend↔backend contracts live in `frontend/src/types/api.ts`; when you change an
47	  engine event/meta shape, update both `engine/v5/events.mjs` (EVENT_TYPES + schema)
48	  and `types/api.ts`.
49	- Timestamps crossing the API boundary are numeric epoch-ms, not SQLite DATETIME
50	  strings (the frontend does time math on them).
51	
52	## Hard rules (violating these breaks the build or the design)
53	
54	1. **Never use Gemini** — in any provider chain (judge, sediment audit, agent
55	   backend). It is structurally excluded in `engine/v5/judge.mjs` and
56	   `engine/v5/backends.mjs`; do not reintroduce it via config or fallback.
57	2. **IDENTITY.md role-mapping table is the source of truth for agents.** The
58	   engine compiles agents by parsing the markdown table whose header contains
59	   `Agent ID` (see `engine/regime-to-cc.mjs::parseIdentityTable`). Do NOT rewrite
60	   a regime's IDENTITY.md into prose (`### Agent N:` bullet lists) — that parses
61	   to **0 agents** and the regime can no longer run.
62	3. **Keep `metadata.json.agentCount` in sync with the compiled count.** The
63	   validator enforces `agentCount === Object.keys(convertRegime(dir).agents).length`.
64	   If you change a regime's role table, update `agentCount` to match.
65	4. **Register every new event type in `engine/v5/events.mjs::EVENT_TYPES`** (and
66	   `schemas/match-event.schema.json`). `EventLog.emit` throws on an unknown type,
67	   which crashes the whole match. This is how mechanism events
68	   (`veto_triggered` / `impeach_triggered` / `edict_triggered`) are wired.
69	5. **All user-supplied path segments go through `safeResolve`** (`server/utils.mjs`)
70	   — no `..` traversal, no dot segments.
71	6. **The write API is async**: `POST` endpoints return an id immediately and spawn
72	   work in the background; never block the HTTP response on a match/tournament.
73	7. **New modules need tests.** Tests must be hermetic — fake every external CLI
74	   and point `HOME` at a temp dir (see `test/integration-event-contract.test.mjs`).
75	8. **Language: English for the engineering surface** (code comments, console/log
76	   strings, agent-facing prompts, UI, engineering docs). Use standard sinological
77	   terms for historical content (Hucker official titles: Secretariat 中书省,
78	   Chancellery 门下省, etc.). Two exceptions stay Chinese because they are
79	   *functional or intentional*, not mixed-language slips:
80	   - the mechanism markers `圣旨 / 诏书 / 弹劾 / 驳回` (detection of Chinese agent
81	     output), `regime-to-cc` ROLE_KEYWORDS + OrgChart matching, and the
82	     `regime-validator` section-header regexes — all parse bilingual data;
83	   - `regimes/**` and `docs/IDENTITY-TEMPLATE.md` — the regimes are intentionally
84	     bilingual (`name.zh`/`name.en`), and the template documents that format.

102	## Concurrency notes (a tournament spawns many processes against shared state)
103	
104	- The shared history DB (`~/.civagent/civagent_history.db`) is opened **lazily**
105	  with a busy timeout; WAL is best-effort and never fatal. Don't move DB open
106	  back to module-import time.
107	- Civs write into a regime's `skills/` dir that is symlinked into live HOMEs —
108	  skill files are written via temp-file + atomic rename. Preserve that.
109	- Always attach an `error` handler to a spawned child whose promise resolves on
110	  `close`, or a spawn failure (ENOENT/EMFILE) hangs `Promise.all` forever.
111	- Pass `maxBuffer` to `spawnSync` for judge/extractor calls — transcripts exceed
112	  the 1 MB default.

30 31 > **A hypothesis**: the political institutions that humanity has experimented with repeatedly over five millennia (centralized autocracy, separation of powers, democratic assembly, federal autonomy, theocratic rule, dual-track checks) are, at their core, historical answers to the problem of **multi-entity collaboration**. If we treat each AI agent as analogous to a "minister," and the problem-solving process as analogous to "governance," then the 57 historical governance systems become 57 **reusable multi-agent orchestration patterns** — each stress-tested in real history over decades, even millennia. 32 > 33 > *"The present is history's laboratory; the past, its ruined library."* 34 > — Michael Oakeshott, *On History* (1983) 35 36 --- 37 38 ## Abstract 39 40 **CivAgent** is a research testbed that treats historical governance systems as formal **multi-agent orchestration patterns** for Large Language Model (LLM) coordination. The system encodes **57 regimes** (20 Chinese dynasties, 37 global empires) — each with a historically grounded role mapping, command hierarchy, and decision flow — and compiles them at runtime into executable agent teams for the Claude Code runtime. Version 6 introduces **The Constitutional Engine** (`[VETO]`, `[IMPEACH]`, `[EDICT]`) for absolute override mechanisms, and a **Real-Time Live Court SSE Dashboard** to visualize these political clashes dynamically. 41 42 This project explores an empirical question: **can the diversity of human political institutions be regarded as a historical answer to the general problem of "multi-agent collaboration"?** If so, then AI agent orchestration need not reinvent the wheel — the Tang Three Departments and Six Ministries, the Roman Republic, the Venetian council, the Byzantine bureaucratic empire, and others are all **already-validated** collaboration topologies that can be invoked directly once formalized. 43 44 --- 45 46 ## 1. Problem Statement 47 48 ### 1.1 Three Structural Dilemmas of Modern LLM Orchestration 49 50 Current mainstream multi-agent frameworks (AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, etc.) face: 51 52 1. **A scarcity of orchestration patterns** — most projects adopt *ad hoc* role assignment (e.g., "coder / reviewer / tester"), lacking any theoretical foundation. When should one use a hierarchy? When a collegial body? When a dual-track system? Decisions have no principled basis. 53 2. **Cross-session amnesia** — agents forget the experience of prior matches every time they restart. Projects such as Hermes Agent have begun to introduce automatic skill accretion, but most frameworks remain stuck at stateless invocation. 54 3. **Homogenization bias** — the "one coordinator + N specialists" structure recurs endlessly, ignoring the far richer collaboration forms found in history (e.g., the Roman dual consulship, the Ming Grand Secretariat–Directorate of Ceremonial dual track, the Persian satrapal federation). 55 56 ### 1.2 Proposition 57 58 > **Proposition**: the 57 governance systems in human history constitute a knowledge base concerning "multi-entity collaboration" that has **already been stress-tested over the long run under real conditions**. Formalizing them as AI agent orchestration patterns can mitigate the three dilemmas above. 59 60 This project is not a game, nor a visualization demo, but a **runnable experimental platform** for validating this proposition. 61 62 --- 63 64 ## 2. Theoretical Framework 65 66 ### 2.1 Regime as Topology 67 68 Drawing on the political-science analyses of Montesquieu (*The Spirit of the Laws*, 1748), Qian Mu (*The Gains and Losses of Chinese Political Institutions Through the Ages*, 1952), and Acemoglu & Robinson (*Why Nations Fail*, 2012), any regime can be abstracted along four dimensions: 69 70 | Dimension | Formalization | Corresponding AI Orchestration Element | 71 |---|---|---| 72 | **Locus of authority** | Single point / distributed / rotating | Single agent / multiple agents / rotating coordinator | 73 | **Decision flow** | Topology of a DAG | Message passing graph | 74 | **Checks & balances** | Distribution of veto power | Review agents with veto | 75 | **Institutional memory** | Archives / oral tradition / legal codes | Persistent skill storage | 76 77 For example, the **Tang Three Departments and Six Ministries** can be formalized as: 78 - Locus of authority: single point (the Emperor) 79 - Decision flow: `Emperor → Secretariat (drafting) → Chancellery (review, may reject) → Department of State Affairs (execution) → Six Ministries in parallel` 80 - Checks & balances: the Chancellery holds the power to reject and return edicts (fengbo) over the Secretariat; the Censorate is independent of the Three Departments 81 - Memory: the *Tang Code with Commentary* (*Tanglü Shuyi*) + the merit-evaluation system 82 83 This maps directly onto Claude Code's `--agents` JSON: 84 - coordinator = emperor 85 - engineering = zhongshu-sheren (drafter) 86 - review = menxia-shiyushi (Attending Censor of the Chancellery) 87 - management = shangshu-ling (Director of the Department of State Affairs) + Six Ministries 88 89 #### 2.1.1 Relation to "Graph Engineering" 90 91 The term **graph engineering** — designing the multi-agent *organization* as a programmable structure (which nodes exist, which transitions are permitted, how runtime work graphs form and mutate) rather than tuning one agent's behavioral loop — spread through the agent-development community in mid-2026. CivAgent is an instance of that discipline, and predates the label: every regime ships a `topology.json` that is a typed directed multigraph, and `engine/topology/metrics.mjs` turns it into numbers (density, command-chain depth, in-degree centrality, count of checks-and-balances cycles). 92 93 What CivAgent contributes to that discipline is the part it is currently missing: **priors and evidence**. Practitioners hand-draw agent graphs with no principled basis for "should there be a reviewer node here?" — the same *scarcity of orchestration patterns* named in §1.1. This project supplies 57 topologies that were stress-tested against reality for decades to millennia, plus a harness (`civagent tournament` + Bradley-Terry ranking + generated controls) that can say whether one wiring actually beats another. 94 95 Two honest caveats, stated up front because they bound every claim below: 96 97 1. **The rankings are over *declared* topologies.** Whether a declared edge was actually traversed during a match is not yet verified — a regime that declares a veto edge and never exercises it is behaviorally a flat topology, but is currently scored as a checked one. 98 2. **Controls isolate topology only if persona is held constant.** An earlier control generator stripped both, which made one smoke run measure persona presence rather than wiring. `engine/baseline.mjs` now copies `SOUL.md` verbatim and rewrites only the decision flow; `test/baseline.test.mjs` guards this. 99 100 ### 2.2 The Six Canonical Orchestration Patterns 101 102 From an abstract inductive analysis of the 57 regimes, V6 adopts the following 6 **canonical patterns**. Each pattern corresponds to an executable specification in `engine/modes/*.md`: 103 104 | Pattern | Topology | Historical Prototype | When to Use | 105 |---|---|---|---| 106 | `centralized` | Star: a single coordinator directly governs N executors | Qin, Roman Empire, Napoleon, USSR | Speed of decision takes priority over deliberation | 107 | `checks-and-balances` | Pipeline + feedback loop: Draft → Review → Execute | Tang Three Departments and Six Ministries, Roman Republic, US Federal | Low reversibility, high cost of error | 108 | `democratic` | Parallel multiple agents + vote aggregation | Athens, Switzerland, Venice | Dispersed preferences, consensus legitimacy matters | 109 | `dual-track` | Two mutually independent execution chains in parallel | Ming Grand Secretariat + Directorate of Ceremonial, Tokugawa Shogunate | Information redundancy and mutual checks needed | 110 | `federation` | Central node + multiple autonomous sub-nodes | Holy Roman Empire, Zhou, Persian satrapies | Highly heterogeneous domains, local autonomy | 111 | `theocratic` | A hierarchy with "ultimate interpretive authority" | Caliphate, Byzantium, the Papacy | Value alignment takes priority over efficiency | 112 113 Each pattern has, in `engine/modes/.md`, three formalized sections — **Execution Flow**, **CC Implementation**, and **When to Use** — that Claude Code can inject via `--append-system-prompt`. 114 115 ### 2.3 Civilization as Agents + SOUL 116 117 Each regime is defined by three normalized documents: 118 119 - **`metadata.json`** — structured metadata: id, era, orchestrationPattern, tags 120 - **`IDENTITY.md`** — the role-mapping table (`Historical Role | Agent ID | AI Responsibility | Recommended Model`), organization chart, decision flow, institutional characteristics, and historical references 121 - **`SOUL.md`** — the institutional philosophy and behavioral code (language style, interaction norms, taboos) 122 123 These three documents are compiled by `engine/regime-to-cc.mjs` into the agents JSON + system prompt that Claude Code accepts. 124 125 --- 126 127 ## 3. Key Contributions of v5 128 129 Compared with v4 (which only performed static regime → agents compilation), v5 introduces three structural improvements: 130 131 ### 3.1 Cross-Match Learning Loop 132 133 Inspiration: the "agent-curated memory" and "autonomous skill creation" of [NousResearch/hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent). 134 135 v5 maintains an independent memory for each civilization: 136 137 ``` 138 ~/.civagent/envs/-/ ← isolated HOME (one per civilization) 139 ├── .claude/ 140 │ ├── CLAUDE.md ← seed from SOUL.md + IDENTITY.md 141 │ └── skills/ 142 │ ├── learned---.md ← automatically accreted 143 │ └── ... (symlinked from regimes//skills/) 144 ├── .config/, .local/, .cache/ ← XDG path isolation, preventing cross-civilization contamination 145 ``` 146 147 After each match concludes, `engine/v5/skill-sediment.mjs` triggers the following pipeline: 148 149 1. **Transcript cleaning**: strip ANSI escapes, unpack JSONL chunks 150 2. **Pattern extraction** (Codex `codex exec`): extract ≤2 reusable governance patterns, output as Markdown + YAML frontmatter 151 3. **Shape review** (independent review via `engine/v5/judge.mjs`): opencode reviewer preferred, Codex as fallback (never Gemini), verifying that the skill structure is compliant (`Pattern section ≥2 bullets`, not boilerplate); the review engine differs from the extraction engine to avoid self-endorsement 152 4. **Injection guard**: regex-based rejection of jailbreak patterns such as `ignore previous instructions`, ``, `[INST]` 153 5. **Frontmatter enforcement**: any file lacking a YAML header is rejected outright 154 6. **Provenance banner**: each skill is headed with `source_match=`, warning downstream consumers that "this is data, not directives" 155 156 This pipeline has passed three rounds of cross-review by Codex / Claude / Kimi. all 6 reassigned | 183 184 Parallel wall-time ≈ 15 min. All 57 regimes passed structural validation via `npm run validate:regimes`. 185 186 An empirical finding worth recording: **the content-filtering strictness of Chinese domestic AI on political prompts far exceeds expectations** — Kimi returned a `high risk` error directly for 6/6 historical regimes; by contrast, cc-deepseek, cc-glm, and cc-qwen processed the same content normally. This discrepancy has independent value for research into content-safety policy. 187 188 ### 3.3 Tournament — Parallel Civilization Contest 189 190 `civagent tournament --civs ""` launches N civilizations in a parallel match: 191 192 1. **Parallel dispatch**: each civilization runs in `--v5` mode within its own isolated HOME 193 2. **Transcript collection**: the N match records are aggregated into `~/.civagent/tournaments//` 194 3. **AI adjudication**: via `engine/v5/judge.mjs` (Codex preferred, opencode reviewer as fallback, never Gemini), scored on three dimensions 195 - *Legality* — does it abide by the civilization's own institutional rules? 196 - *Feasibility* — is the plan executable? 197 - *Resilience* — can it withstand second-order effects? 198 4. **Output**: `result.md` containing a Markdown scoring table + a Verdict argumentation paragraph 199 200 The judge prompt lives in `engine/v5/tournament.mjs::JUDGE_PROMPT`, and can be customized to replace it with a multi-judge voting mechanism. 201 202 ### 3.4 V6.0 Full-Stack Engineering Overhaul (The Digital Humanities Platform) 203 204 In the major refactor of the **v6.0 release**, CivAgent completed its leap from a "command-line toy" to a "full-stack digital humanities platform": 205 206 1. **Pluggable Mechanism Engine (Constitutional Mechanisms)**: 207 The core engine's hard-coded logic (such as the VETO sniffer) was extracted into a standalone `engine/mechanisms/veto.mjs`, providing a standard plugin interface for future historical game mechanisms (such as "impeachment," "court deliberation," and "abdication"). When an agent holding review authority (such as the Tang Chancellery) emits a `[VETO]` signal, the engine triggers a `SIGKILL`-level fengbo (edict rejection) precisely through the mechanism system. 208 2. **Microservice Backend (Express Microservices)**: 209 The monolithic, bloated Server was thoroughly discarded, decomposed into a `server/routes/` routing architecture, and `server/db/database.mjs` (based on `better-sqlite3`) was introduced as a high-speed time-series database foundation. It fully adheres to the principle of "zero external runtime dependencies" (depending only on Node.js and SQLite). 210 3. **Premium Large-Screen Frontend (Glassmorphism Dashboard)**: 211 The frontend architecture was rebuilt as a React SPA, removing redundant libraries. It adopts the highly contemporary **Glassmorphism** visual paradigm, native Vanilla CSS, and a built-in SVG rendering engine. It provides **Empire-Wide Monitoring (Overview)**, the **Power-Topology Dashboard (Analytics)**, and the **Time-Series Memory Browser (Memory)**, elevating dull AI match logs into a visually striking epic scroll. 212 213 ### 3.5 The Experimental-Validity Layer (post-v6 iterations R5–R7) 214 215 v6 made the platform runnable. The iterations after it were aimed at a narrower question: **are the numbers this platform produces worth anything?** A ranking of governance topologies is only as good as the harness that produced it, so this layer is deliberately unglamorous. 216 217 1. **Write path and scenario library.** `POST /api/tournaments` (`server/routes/tournaments.mjs`) lets the dashboard start a real contest instead of only reading finished ones; `engine/prompts/governance-scenarios.json` holds 40 governance scenarios so a match is drawn from a fixed corpus rather than an ad-hoc prompt. 218 219 2. **Blind, calibrated, multi-judge scoring** (`engine/v5/judge.mjs`, `judge-rubric.mjs`, `judge-calibration.mjs`). Transcripts are anonymized — regime ids, topology node labels and IDENTITY agent ids are all rewritten to `Civ-A-Rn` slots, since leaving a single office name in place tells the judge exactly which dynasty it is reading. Scoring uses an anchored 4-point rubric per dimension, two passes with the presentation order swapped, and up to three providers (`codex`, `opencode-reviewer`, `cn-glm`). The result carries a `biasReport`: per-provider mean and variance, same-model-family versus cross-family score gap, and the per-pass position effect. Transcripts are truncated to a shared verbosity budget, because otherwise the ranking partly measures which civilization wrote more. 220 221 3. **Generated controls** (`engine/baseline.mjs`). Three variants per regime — `solo` (one office), `flat-N` (same offices, zero edges), `random-N` (same offices and edge-kind distribution, seeded scrambled wiring). Controls copy `SOUL.md` verbatim and keep every office id, label and duty; only the decision-flow prose and the mermaid diagram are rewritten. Varying persona and topology together is the failure mode this design exists to prevent (see §2.1.1). 222 223 4. **Episodic memory retrieval** (`engine/v5/history-db.mjs`, `history-retriever.mjs`). Past matches are queried by keyword with stopword filtering, ordered newest-first with a deterministic tie-break — `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` is second-granular, so matches recorded in the same second would otherwise come back in arbitrary order. 224 225 5. **Transcript capture** (`engine/v5/stream-json.mjs`). A regime's offices are Claude Code subagents; under the default `text` output format their deliberation never reached the transcript, and the judge scored whatever the coordinator happened to restate. The backend now streams structured events, rendered back to plain text with per-office attribution. Constitutional signals are matched as bracketed markers only — `[VETO]`, `[EDICT]`, `[IMPEACH: x]` — because the bare words *驳回*, *诏书* and *圣旨* appear as ordinary vocabulary in 33 of the 57 regime files, and a regime describing its own constitution must not be read as exercising it. 226 227 6. **Transcript selection for judging** (`engine/v5/events.mjs`). The judge used to read `text.slice(-6000)` — a blind tail. Harmless when transcripts were kilobytes; after capture was fixed a Tang match runs to 72,830 characters, and the tail contained *none* of the Secretariat's, Chancellery's or Department of State Affairs' segments. Selection is now actor-stratified, and the per-civ record states what never reached the judge (67,867 characters on that match) rather than reporting only what was kept. 228 229 7. **Dispatch plan and enforcement** (`engine/v5/dispatch-plan.mjs`, `plan-diff.mjs`). The coordinator first states, with tools disabled, which offices it would call; enforcement then requires the offices that are targets of incoming edges in that arm's *own* topology — identically for a historical regime and for its scrambled control. The pre-enforcement plan measures voluntary adoption; only post-enforcement output is eligible for a quality comparison. Participation is recorded as `observed` / `not_observed` / `unknown`, never as an execution rate. 230 231 8. **Graph metrics and topology validation** (`engine/topology/`). Every regime's `topology.json` is schema-checked and cross-checked against its IDENTITY role table, then reduced to density, command-chain depth, in-degree centrality and checks-and-balances cycle count. 232 233 9. **Replay and skill accounting** (`engine/v5/replay.mjs`, `skill-outcome.mjs`, `skill-quality.mjs`). A past match can be re-run with the same regime, backend and task; learned skills are deduplicated by content hash and stamped with the tournament outcome they participated in, since the extractor itself is structurally blind to whether the match was won or lost. 234 235 --- 236 237 ## 4. Limitations 654 655 ### 9.1 Institutional Compression 656 657 Compressing an entire governance system into a single `SOUL.md` + role-mapping table inevitably loses dimensions such as the inter-departmental tensions inside the institution, informal power networks, and generational evolution. For example: 658 659 - The Tang **regional military governors** (*jiedushi*) and their tensions with the center are difficult to express within a single SOUL 660 - The Byzantine **factional politics** (Blues / Greens) is not represented 661 - Whether the Soviet **Party–state dual track** should be modeled as `centralized` or `dual-track` is a matter of theoretical dispute 662 663 **v5.2 plan**: split each regime into multiple sub-regimes (e.g., `tang-early` / `tang-mid` / `tang-late`, or subdivided by department into independent agent teams). 664 665 ### 9.2 Temporal Dimension 666 667 The `regimes/` directory places ancient dynasties and modern nation-states side by side (`china/tang` next to `us-federal`), with no chronological validation. This is **intentional design** (to support cross-era analogies), but it must be flagged explicitly in scholarly analysis. 668 669 ### 9.3 AI-Authored Content 670 671 The 57 IDENTITY.md files were rewritten in parallel by 9 AI pipelines, and their historical accuracy has not been verified item by item by domain experts. v5.0.1 found 5 actual errors through 3 rounds of sample review: 672 673 | Civilization | Issue | Status | 674 |---|---|---| 675 | tang | `司礼监` (Directorate of Ceremonial) is a Ming–Qing agency; the Tang had no such office | ✅ Fixed to `中书舍人` (Secretariat Drafter) in v5.0.1 | 676 | byzantine | `theokrator` is not a standard title; the Patriarch's ethical veto over the Basileus is exaggerated | Pending fix in v5.1 | 677 | roman-republic | The ASCII chart is too linear; the Comitia should be placed above the Consul | Pending fix in v5.1 | 678 | prussia | The entire 1701–1918 period is compressed into a single chart; `Ober-Kriegsrat` may be fictitious | Pending fix in v5.1 | 679 | ottoman | `Nişancı` is mistranslated as "Lord Chief Justice" (should be the tuğra authentication officer) | Pending fix in v5.1 | 680 681 See [regimes/REVIEW-FINDINGS-v5.md](./regimes/REVIEW-FINDINGS-v5.md) for details. 682 683 ### 9.4 CN Model Content Filtering 684 685 Empirical finding: `cc-kimi` returned `API Error: 400 "high risk"` directly for all 6 of its assigned historical-regime prompts (including neutral historical descriptions discussing the Ming Grand Secretariat and the Joseon dynasty). The other CN backends (deepseek / glm / qwen / doubao) processed the same content normally. This discrepancy reflects different vendors' content-safety policies and is a useful reference for projects using Chinese models at scale. 686 687 ### 9.5 Residual Judging Bias 688 689 Multi-judge blind scoring now exists (§3.5): anonymized transcripts, an anchored 4-point rubric, order-swapped passes, up to three providers, a shared verbosity budget, and a `biasReport` covering per-provider variance, same-family versus cross-family score gaps, and position effects. That hedges the three biases the literature names — position, verbosity, self-preference — but **hedging is not elimination**, and the report exists so the residue stays visible rather than getting averaged away. 690 691 Known residue: 692 693 - **The judge pool is small and correlated.** Three providers, all instruction-tuned frontier models; agreement between them is weaker evidence than it looks. 694 - **Rubric anchoring is itself a prior.** "Legality / feasibility / resilience" encodes a view of what good governance output is. A regime optimized for a dimension the rubric omits scores badly for reasons that have nothing to do with its topology. 695 - **Length control is blunt.** Truncating to a shared budget removes the crudest verbosity advantage, but a civilization that answers in a dense summary and one that answers in full prose are still not being compared like for like. 696 697 ### 9.6 Declared vs. Exercised Topology 698 699 Every ranking in this project is over a *declared* graph. `civagent runtime-graph --diff` now reconstructs what actually happened from the event stream's span tree and compares it against the declared topology — and the first thing it establishes is that **the comparison cannot yet be made at office level**. 700 701 Until recently the comparison could not be made at all: the backend was spawned with `-p` and the default `text` output format, which prints only the coordinator's final assistant message, so every office's deliberation was discarded before it reached the event stream. Turns were tagged with the regime id because that was the only identity available. 702 703 That is fixed. The backend now runs with `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, and `engine/v5/stream-json.mjs` renders the stream back to plain text while keeping the dispatch mapping — a delegation carries `input.subagent_type`, the reply carries `parent_tool_use_id` — so turns are attributed as `china/tang#menxia`. On one verification run the same regime and scenario went from 579 captured characters to 72,830, with all three departments visible and the Chancellery's three rounds of *fengbo* review in the transcript. 704 705 **The remaining gap is narrower, and now precisely located.** `civagent runtime-graph --diff` reconstructs at office level and reports what is genuinely observable: which offices spoke, how often, and the coordinator's dispatch sequence. What it still cannot observe is the thing the declared topology actually specifies — a *typed, directed* edge between two offices. Claude Code subagents do not call each other; the coordinator relays every hand-off, so a `menxia → zhongshu [veto]` edge is physically indistinguishable from `coordinator → menxia` followed by `coordinator → zhongshu`. Closing this needs the event stream to record the logical producer of each hand-off, not just the physical one. 706 707 So `unexercised_ratio` stays `null`, and — importantly — so do `total_unexercised` and `edge_exercise_counts`. "Unexercised" is a claim about behaviour, and in the verification match the Chancellery demonstrably *did* review the Secretariat's draft three times: those edges were exercised and merely invisible. Reporting them as unexercised would be false, so the same list is published as `unobservable_edges` instead. Treat topology-level conclusions as claims about declarations rather than about behaviour. 708 709 Full audit report: [regimes/AUDIT.md](./regimes/AUDIT.md) 710 711 --- 712 713 ### 9.7 What the Experiments Have Actually Shown 714 715 Two pilots have been run and both are recorded in `docs/experiments/`, including the outcomes that count against this project's own proposition. 716 717 **E1** (5 regimes × 3 scenarios, no control arm) could not be interpreted: score tracked transcript length with Spearman ρ = +1.00 on the one scenario whose spread exceeded the judge's noise, and the three lowest-scoring cells were the three whose transcripts were missing most of the work. That run is superseded — it predates the capture fix. 718 719 **E1-control** (5 source/control pairs × 3 scenarios) was scored against pre-registered rules: historical wiring won **0** resolved pairs, the seeded random rewiring won 1, 5 were inside the judge's own noise, and 9 were excluded. The exclusions are the finding: **in 14 of 30 arms the regime never called a single office**, so neither topology was exercised. Delegation turned out to be driven by the scenario (plague 10/10 delegated, militarization 2/10) rather than by the constitution, and source and control arms failed to delegate at exactly the same rate — 7/15 each. 720 721 So the honest status is: **no claim that governance topology affects multi-agent performance is supported yet, and neither is the opposite.** The obstacle moved from "the harness discards the deliberation" (fixed) to "the regimes frequently do not deliberate", which §3.5's dispatch plan and enforcement exist to separate. E2 is designed and pre-registered at `docs/experiments/E2-preregistration.md`; it has not been run. 722 723 --- 724 725 ## 10. 1	# Athenian Democracy / 雅典民主 — Direct Democracy / 直接民主制
2	
3	> 508-322 BC · Direct Democracy / 直接民主制
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 一、历史背景 / Historical Background
8	
9	公元前508年，克里斯提尼（Cleisthenes）推翻了庇西特拉图家族的僭主统治，实施了一场彻底的政治改革，开创了人类历史上第一个民主政体。他打破了传统的四部落制，重新划分为十个部落（phylai），每个部落混合了城市、沿海和内陆的居民，从根本上瓦解了贵族氏族的权力基础。议事会（Boule）由500人组成，每部落50人，通过抽签选出，任期一年，负责为公民大会准备议程。
10	
11	In 508 BC, Cleisthenes overthrew the Peisistratid tyranny and enacted a radical political transformation, creating humanity's first democratic government. He dismantled the traditional four tribes, reorganizing citizens into ten new tribes (phylai), each mixing urban, coastal, and inland residents — fundamentally destroying the power base of aristocratic clans. The Council (Boule) of 500, with 50 members from each tribe chosen by lot for one-year terms, prepared the agenda for the Assembly.
12	
13	公元前462年，厄菲阿尔特斯（Ephialtes）进一步削弱了贵族会议（Areopagus）的权力，将其大部分职能转移给公民大会和陪审法庭。其后伯里克利（Pericles，约前495-429年）引领雅典进入黄金时代：帕特农神庙拔地而起，悲剧诗人索福克勒斯和欧里庇得斯的杰作问世，苏格拉底在集市上论辩，修昔底德撰写历史。伯里克利最重要的改革之一是为公共服务提供薪酬（misthos），使贫穷公民也能参与政治。
14	
15	In 462 BC, Ephialtes further stripped the aristocratic Areopagus of its powers, transferring most functions to the Assembly and people's courts. Pericles (c. 495-429 BC) then led Athens into its Golden Age: the Parthenon rose on the Acropolis, Sophocles and Euripides created tragic masterpieces, Socrates debated in the agora, and Thucydides wrote history. Pericles' crucial reform of providing pay for public service (misthos) enabled even poor citizens to participate in politics.
16	
17	雅典民主的独特之处在于其"直接"性质——不存在代议制。约3万-4万成年男性公民有权在公民大会（Ekklesia）上发言和投票，每年至少召开40次。陶片放逐法（Ostracism）允许公民投票放逐任何被认为威胁民主的个人，任期十年。公民大会的决定对所有人具有约束力，包括将军和执政官。这种制度持续运行近两百年，直到公元前322年马其顿征服后被废止。
18	
19	Athenian democracy was uniquely "direct" — there was no representative system. Approximately 30,000-40,000 adult male citizens had the right to speak and vote in the Assembly (Ekklesia), which met at least 40 times annually. Ostracism allowed citizens to vote to exile anyone deemed a threat to democracy for ten years. Assembly decisions bound everyone, including generals and magistrates. This system operated for nearly two centuries until its abolition following the Macedonian conquest in 322 BC.
20	
21	雅典民主对西方政治思想产生了深远影响。亚里士多德在《政治学》中系统分析了其优缺点，波利比乌斯将其与罗马共和制进行比较，美国建国之父在制定宪法时反复引用雅典的经验教训。尽管以现代标准衡量，雅典民主排斥了女性、奴隶和外邦人，但其核心理念——公民平等参与公共事务——至今仍是民主理论的基石。
22	
23	Athenian democracy profoundly influenced Western political thought. Aristotle systematically analyzed its strengths and weaknesses in *Politics*, Polybius compared it with the Roman Republic, and America's Founding Fathers repeatedly cited Athenian lessons when drafting their Constitution. Though by modern standards Athenian democracy excluded women, slaves, and foreign residents (metics), its core idea — equal citizen participation in public affairs — remains the cornerstone of democratic theory.
24	
25	## 二、制度设计详解 / System Design
26	
27	### 核心架构 / Core Architecture
28	
29	雅典民主的核心机构包括：公民大会（Ekklesia）是最高权力机关，所有公民均可参与投票；议事会（Boule of 500）负责议程准备和日常行政；十将军（Strategoi）是唯一通过选举而非抽签产生的重要官职，负责军事指挥；执政官（Archons）负责行政和宗教事务；陪审法庭（Dikasterion）由数百至数千名陪审员组成，审理案件并执行法律；演说家（Rhetores）虽非正式官职，但在辩论中发挥关键的舆论引导作用。
30	
31	The core institutions of Athenian democracy included: the Assembly (Ekklesia) as the supreme authority where all citizens could vote; the Council (Boule of 500) for agenda preparation and daily administration; the ten Generals (Strategoi) — the only major office filled by election rather than lot — commanding the military; Archons handling administrative and religious duties; the People's Court (Dikasterion), with juries of hundreds to thousands, trying cases and enforcing law; and Orators (Rhetores), who, though not formal officeholders, played a crucial role in shaping public opinion through debate.
32	
33	### 组织架构图 / Organization Chart
34	
35	```

37	              │    🏛️ 公民大会        │
38	              │     Ekklesia         │
39	              │  (Supreme Assembly)  │
40	              │  所有公民投票 / All    │
41	              │  citizens vote       │
42	              └──────────┬───────────┘
43	                         │
44	          ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
